newsitem.title: GERMANY: GRUNDIG COULD FACE BANKRUPTCY IN 97-UNION.
newsitem.headline: GRUNDIG COULD FACE BANKRUPTCY IN 97-UNION.

text.p: Troubled home electronics maker Grundig AG could face bankruptcy this summer unless it finds a new business partner, representatives of the IG Metall union said on Wednesday.
Grundig has been looking for a company willing to invest in its German plants since Philips Electronics NV gave up control of the stereo and television maker January 1.

Grundig would know within a week if it could take legal action accusing Philips of ruining Grundig to promote its own lines of electronics, said Gerd Loboda, a union leader and chairman of Grundig's supervisory board, said.
"Everything that Philips does shows that Philips wants to have Grundig out of the market," Loboda said.
Last month Grundig, which lost an estimated 350 million marks ($212.8 million) last year, paid Philips 250 million marks in connection with the cancellation of the options.

Philips was seeking to dissolve its contract under which it pays 45 million marks per year to a foundation controlled by the heirs of founder Max Grundig, Philips CFO Dudley Eustace said earlier on Wednesday in the daily Sueddeutsche Zeitung.
The pact gave Philips control of Grundig even though it held only a 32 percent stake and options to buy the foundation's 68 percent holding.
Eustace blamed Grundig's woes on the high cost of manufacturing in Germany.
-- Neal Boudette, Bonn Newsroom, +49-228 260976150 ($ = 1.645 German Marks) 051239 GMT feb 97
